final_task_tree.title: Figure out a training plan for my dog
final_task_tree.description:
Rescue border collie mix, 14 months. Pulls hard on the leash and barks at every other dog on walks. South Bay, California; I can do evenings and weekends.

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

subtasks.title: Decide: hire a trainer vs. DIY for leash pulling + dog reactivity
subtasks.description: Answer one question: for a 14-month rescue border collie mix that pulls hard and barks at every dog it sees, is this a DIY-with-good-resources problem or a hire-a-pro problem? Reactivity specifically is the deciding factor — look at whether reactivity is generally considered self-trainable or whether a pro is recommended, and what the failure modes of DIY are. Output: a clear recommendation with reasoning, written into this description.

subtasks.title: Find 2-3 South Bay trainers who handle leash reactivity, with real prices
subtasks.description: Find actual local options serving the South Bay (San Jose / Sunnyvale / Santa Clara / Mountain View / Campbell area). Requirements: positive-reinforcement / force-free methods, explicitly handle leash reactivity or dog-dog reactivity, and offer evening or weekend availability. Must capture real dollar prices, not 'contact us'. Record name, method, service format (private/group/board), price, phone, website, and what's included.

subtasks.title: Write the week-by-week plan for weeks 1-4
subtasks.description: Build a four-week plan the owner can start this weekend, covering both problems: loose-leash walking and dog reactivity. Must fit evenings + weekends only. Each week needs: the goal, the specific drills, roughly how long per session, and how to tell if it's working. Include the gear needed up front.
